families.name: Procurement competition and bidding patterns
families.what: How open and normal the tender was: number of bidders, how close the winning bid was to the ceiling, how fast the award came.

indicators.label: Very fast award: 8 days or less after bid opening
indicators.evidence: Termination odds ×2.1 (1.5–2.9); held on 2023–2025 (×2.6)

indicators.label: Winning bid unusually low: 94% of the official budget or less
indicators.evidence: Termination odds ×4.4 (3.1–6.1); held on 2023–2025

indicators.label: One bidder and winning bid 98%+ of the budget
indicators.evidence: Citizen-report odds ×1.5 (1.2–2.0); not linked to termination

indicators.label: One or two bidders
indicators.evidence: Citizen-report odds ×1.5; termination not higher, so not scored

families.name: Project cost and cost anomalies
families.what: Whether the official budget is high for the work: price per km against the same type of work, nationally, with a regional cost factor for context.

indicators.label: Price per km at or above the 95th percentile of similar works
indicators.evidence: Termination odds ×2.95 (1.44–6.02) with the v0.10 groups and 200 m floor

indicators.label: Price per km between the 90th and 95th percentile
indicators.evidence: A milder version of the same pattern

indicators.label: Total budget above the 95th percentile when the length is not stated
indicators.evidence: Fallback when price per km cannot be computed

indicators.label: Regional cost factor (DPWH regional prices differ)
indicators.evidence: Factor 0.80–1.25 by region; tested as an adjustment, did not sharpen the link, so shown only

indicators.label: Works under 200 m are not priced per km
indicators.evidence: Short segments carry fixed costs; removing them raised the price signal's odds ratio

families.name: Contractor history and performance
families.what: The bidders' track record on earlier DPWH road contracts, official sanctions, and citizen inspections of their work.

indicators.label: A bidder had an earlier contract terminated
indicators.evidence: Winner with a termination: termination odds ×2.1 (1.6–2.8); held on 2023–2025

indicators.label: Bidder on the GPPB blacklist, or licence marked [REVOKED]
indicators.evidence: Official record (verify the name match)

indicators.label: Winner's other projects drew 2+ citizen reports
indicators.evidence: Citizen-report odds ×4.5 (3.7–5.4)

indicators.label: Bisto.ph inspectors rated the winner's work unsatisfactory
indicators.evidence: Citizen inspection record

indicators.label: Earlier termination rate 5%+ (5+ earlier contracts)
indicators.evidence: Termination odds ×4.0 overall; not confirmed on 2023–2025

families.name: Contractor ownership, affiliation and bidding networks
families.what: Who is behind the bidders and who they bid with: official actions, reported company–person links, name matches to officials or offshore records, office concentration, repeat co-bidders.

indicators.label: Bidder named in an official action (referral, charge, COA finding, suspension)
indicators.evidence: Compiled from public sources; status as reported

indicators.label: Bidder has a documented link to an official or investigation
indicators.evidence: From the team's sourced register; reported, not proven

indicators.label: Name matches a politically exposed person or an offshore record
indicators.evidence: OpenSanctions PEPs, ICIJ Offshore Leaks; namesakes are common

indicators.label: Winner holds 50%+ of the district office's contracts
indicators.evidence: Too few past cases to test

indicators.label: Bidders who met in 3+ earlier tenders; alternating wins
indicators.evidence: Not linked to termination (odds ×0.5); citizen reports ×1.3

families.name: Political economy and power concentration
families.what: How concentrated political power is where the road is: political families in elective office and the district representative's family, from documented relations.

indicators.label: Dynasty share of the province's elected local positions (Ateneo dataset, 2016)
indicators.evidence: High-dynasty provinces: termination odds ×1.35, citizen reports ×1.57, but the link flips within poorer vs richer provinces, so context only

indicators.label: Current officials with documented relatives in office (Wikidata)
indicators.evidence: Updates the 2016 Ateneo picture for 2019–2025 terms; partial coverage

indicators.label: District representative's relatives in elective office
indicators.evidence: Shown for the reviewer; never used to link a contractor without a documented source

indicators.label: Documented link between a bidder and an official
indicators.evidence: Counted under ownership and affiliation

families.name: Implementation delays and performance anomalies
families.what: What happens after award: progress against the plan, time overruns, and what citizens and inspectors report on site.

indicators.label: Possibly stalled: 1+ year past the planned end with under 50% done
indicators.evidence: Weekly list of on-going roads; not scored yet (DPWH progress data can lag)

indicators.label: Citizens reported this project on the DPWH portal
indicators.evidence: Public reports (ghost, defective, unfinished)

indicators.label: Bisto.ph inspectors rated this project unsatisfactory
indicators.evidence: Citizen inspection record

backtest.verdict: linked to worse outcomes: candidate for scoring after team review
linked to worse outcomes: candidate for scoring after team review

sources.name: DPWH project records
sources.what: Every DPWH project: status, budget, contractor, bidders, dates, official bid price (via the BetterGov public API)

sources.name: Tender documents
sources.what: Bidding documents linked from DPWH records, read (with OCR for scans) and checked by Claude

sources.name: GPPB blacklist
sources.what: Government blacklist of suppliers and contractors (via OpenSanctions)

sources.name: Bisto.ph
sources.what: Citizen site inspections with satisfactory / unsatisfactory ratings

sources.name: DPWH citizen reports
sources.what: Number of public reports filed against each project

sources.name: Politically exposed persons
sources.what: Philippine officials and politicians (OpenSanctions PEP list)

sources.name: PhilGEPS open data
sources.what: Quarterly bulk files of every government tender and award (mPhilGEPS and legacy PhilGEPS): official budget, dates, procurement mode, contract amount, notice to proceed, awardee; matched to DPWH contracts by Contract ID

sources.name: Ateneo Political Dynasties Dataset
sources.what: Every elected local official 2004–2016 with a dynasty flag, provincial dynasty shares, poverty and HDI (Ateneo Policy Center)

sources.name: Elected officials and political families
sources.what: Who holds elective office by province, with documented family relations between officials (Wikidata, CC0); the Ateneo Political Dynasty Database when added

sources.name: Past bidder lists
sources.what: Which firms bid against each other in earlier DPWH tenders (bidding-network context)

sources.name: Regional cost factor
sources.what: How prices for similar road works differ by region, from 2020–2025 DPWH contracts

sources.name: Official actions and documented links
sources.what: Referrals, charges, COA findings and reported company–person links, each with a public source; compiled by the team
